includes_unsettled.answer: Not quantified. The accrual is described as covering all the opioid 'matters described below', which include still-pending unsettled suits, but no filing says how much (if any) is reserved for parties that have not settled, and management says it cannot estimate further losses. FY2020's accrual covered only the cash component of the Settlement Framework; private-plaintiff claims and the non-cash components were not accrued.

quotes.quote: The NOSA does not address claims by private parties, which includes unions and other health and welfare funds, hospital systems and other healthcare providers, businesses, and individuals alleging personal injury. To date, there are approximately 73 lawsuits brought by private plaintiffs pending.
Through July 2026, we have paid the Settling Governmental Entities approximately $2.6 billion and we expect to pay Settling Governmental Entities additional amounts up to $3.7 billion through 2038.

The amount of ultimate loss may differ materially from this accrual, whether as a result of settlement discussions, a judicial decision or verdict or otherwise, but we are not able to estimate a range of reasonably possible additional losses for these matters.
We had $6.73 billion accrued at June 30, 2021 related to certain opioid litigation, including the Proposed Settlement Agreement
We are unable to reasonably estimate the liability or cost associated with the other components of the Settlement Framework ... The Settlement Framework does not address claims by private plaintiffs

JHX.why: AICF annual payments are variable: they depend on JHX free cash flow (as defined in the AFFA), actuarial estimates, claims actually paid, AICF costs, AUD/USD and an annual cash-flow cap. The liability is KPMG's undiscounted actuarial central estimate of future claims through 2074, not a settled amount on a fixed schedule. The FY2026 10-K and FY2025 20-F do not state the 35% FCF percentage; it was not verified from the AFFA exhibit.
JHX.quote: The amount of these annual payments is dependent on several factors, including our free cash flow (as defined in the AFFA), actuarial estimations, actual claims paid, operating expenses of AICF, changes in the AUD/USD exchange rate and the annual cash flow cap.
JHX.filing: JHX 10-K FY2026 (FYE 2026-03-31, filed 2026-05-19), Item 1/MD&A, Consolidated Balance Sheets, Note 12
